thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Struggle For Altitude As Midterms, Fed Meeting Loom

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Struggle For Altitude As Midterms, Fed Meeting Loom
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
Iranian oil-export sanctions take effect
U.S. stocks were mixed out of the gate Monday, in a week set to be teeming with news, including an updated policy statement from the Federal Reserve and midterm elections that could alter the balance of power in Washington.
How did benchmarks fare?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was virtually unchanged at 25273.20 and the S&P 500 was down 4.14 points to 2,718.57, or a decline of 0.2%. The Nasdaq Composite Index fell 99 points, or 1.35% to 7,300.
On Friday, the Dow lost 109.91 points, or 0.4%, to end at 25,270.83, the S&P 500 index fell 17.31 points, or 0.6%, to 2,723.06, and the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 77.06 points, or 1%, to 7,356.99.
For the week, both the Dow and the S&P 500 rose 2.4% and the Nasdaq advanced 2.7%, its first weekly gain since the end of September.
What drove the market?
Midterm congressional elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, take place Tuesday. On Thursday, the Fed concludes a two-day policy meeting, which isn't expected to deliver a change in rates, but may offer fresh insights to investors about the pace of coming rate increases and the effects of trade clashes between the U.S. and China on the domestic economy.
On Friday, markets contended with a series of conflicting headlines on the progress of negotiations between Beijing and Washington. Stocks pared losses in late trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-cuts-intraday-loss-after-trump-declares-progress-on-trade-deal-with-china-directly-countering-kudlow-2018-11-02) Friday after President Donald Trump said progress was being made in talks with Chinese leadership. A few hours earlier, his top economic adviser, Larry Kudlow, said the U.S. and China were a long way from reaching a trade deal.
On Monday, China's President Xi Jinping, speaking at a trade expo in Shangha (https://www.bbc.com/news/business-46093478)i, vowed to address criticisms that its trade practices are "unfair," by reducing its tariffs and opening up its economy to more imports.
The Caixin survey of Chinese manufacturing slipped to 50.8, marking its lowest reading (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/11/05/chinas-services-sector-growth-slowest-in-13-months-caixin-survey.html) in more than a year, supporting the idea that the economy of the world's second-largest economy is slowing. A reading of at least 50 indicates improving conditions.
Read:How U.S.-China trade talks are the biggest catalyst for the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-chart-shows-why-trade-war-fears-are-the-biggest-catalyst-for-the-stock-market-2018-11-02)
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) shares were down 9% in early trade Monday following the iPhone maker's 6.6% stock decline on Friday, after saying it would no longer disclose (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-the-going-gets-tough-apple-hides-its-numbers-2018-11-01) unit sales of its products for investors, as it has for more than a decade.
Under Armour Inc. (UAA) stock is trading up 0.6%, after analysts at Stifel Nicolaus upgraded their price target for the firm to $30, from $27.
Shares of Sysco Corp. (SYY) are falling more than 10% Monday morning, after the company missed earnings estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sysco-shares-slide-6-premarket-after-earnings-miss-2018-11-05) for the first fiscal quarter of 2019.
Cabot Oil & Gas Corp., (COG) rose 4.9% and EQT Corp. advanced more than 7% as natural-gas prices rose sharply on forecasts turning toward colder weather then previously expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05)across much of the U.S. later this month. December natural-gas futures surged 7.5% and hit a 9-month high.
Shares of home-improvement retailer Lowe's Companies(LOW) were off 0.7% after the company said it would close 20 underperforming stored in the U.S. and 31 stores in Canada (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lowes-to-close-51-stores-including-20-in-the-us-2018-11-05) as part of a strategic reassessment.
Read:These Lowe's stores are closing in the next three months (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-lowes-stores-are-closing-in-the-next-three-months-2018-11-05)
Ferrari NV(RACE) stock fell 2% in early trade, following the Monday morning announcement of higher third-quarter profits. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05)
What data are in focus
The Markit services industry index came in at 54.8 for October, versus expectations of 54.7, according to FactSet.
The ISM services index slipped to 60.3 in October (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-economy-still-running-strong-in-october-ism-services-survey-shows-2018-11-05), down from 61.6 in September, but beating the 58.6 average estimate of economists surveyed by MarketWatch.
What are analysts saying?
Ed Yardeni, president and chief investment strategist at Yardeni Research points out that the S&P 500 has risen more than 3% from its low on Oct. 29.
"Is this the beginning of Relief Rally #62, which will take the S&P 500 to new record highs as previous relief rallies have done? We think so," he wrote in a note to clients, though he also said that he is lowering his year-end forecast for the S&P 500 from 3100 to 2900, or in line with September's record high.
"This adds weight to the argument that China's economy is cooling. Overnight, China's Xi Jinping talked about boosting global trade, and warned about the downside of protectionist policies, but the update failed to boost investor sentiment," wrote David Madden, market analyst at CMC Markets UK, in a Monday research note.
